cim: Major tech outages disrupt banks, airlines, federal agencies — senator warns more could be coming
cim_eredeti: Major tech outages disrupt banks, airlines, federal agencies — senator warns more could be coming
szoveg_eredeti:
A series of major technology outages struck systems millions of Americans rely on — from bank accounts to air travel — and Virginia Sen. Mark Warner is warning there could be more disruptions ahead.

Over the course of just a few days, some of the country’s most critical systems went offline.

Warner says there is no evidence the outages were the result of cyberattacks. Instead, he says new artificial intelligence tools are finding security weaknesses faster than companies can fix them — creating a race to update software that some systems simply aren’t built to handle.

“You can almost think about it as leaks and pipes. Not a direct analogy. But where it used to be you’d have one leak a month or every three months. You may have a hundred leaks in a single day,” Warner said. “And if you’re suddenly trying to put all of the patches on at once, you’re not, in some cases, testing the patches quick enough.”

Warner says the FAA ground stop was a separate issue — tied to equipment upgrades rather than artificial intelligence. Still, he says the broader pattern of outages is cause for concern.

While the security updates are meant to make systems safer in the long run, Warner warns the public should brace for continued disruptions as companies scramble to make the changes AI is detecting.

“So, we are going to go through a period of, I fear, outages as companies try to patch quickly,” Warner said. “At the end of the day, our systems will be safer.”

Beyond the outages themselves, Warner says the bigger risk may be what happens to public confidence in artificial intelligence if the disruptions continue — or get worse.

“And my fear is that I think there are still enormous value coming from artificial intelligence and innovation and productivity,” Warner said. “But should we have more of these outages without warning? Or God forbid we have a rogue AI agent go out and do things the way the open AI agent went against this company hugging phase. Or we have an AI-generated cyber-attack, then I think the American people are going to say, hey, we’re done with this. We don’t want to take these risks. So let’s put a risk system in place.”

Warner says establishing a risk framework for AI is a priority.
